question: Which primary embryonic vesicle gives rise to the telencephalon and diencephalon?
explanation: The prosencephalon is the forebrain vesicle that further subdivides during development into the telencephalon and diencephalon. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the adult brain structure that develops directly from the embryonic myelencephalon?
explanation: The myelencephalon is the most caudal secondary vesicle of the hindbrain, which matures to form the medulla oblongata. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which structure connects the left and right cerebral hemispheres to allow interhemispheric communication?
explanation: The corpus callosum is a large bundle of commissural white matter fibers linking the two cerebral hemispheres. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h2)

question: A patient suffering a stroke in the occipital lobe will most likely experience deficits in which function?
explanation: The occipital lobe houses the primary visual cortex, making it the central hub for processing visual information from the eyes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which sensory modality does NOT synapse in the thalamus before reaching the cerebral cortex?
explanation: Smell signals travel directly from the nasal cavity to the olfactory bulb, bypassing the thalamic relay station. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary role of the thalamus in central nervous system function?

options.A: Coordinating balance and fine motor movement
options.B: Relaying and sorting sensory signals to the cortex
options.C: Producing cerebrospinal fluid within the ventricles
options.D: Directly regulating core body temperature and thirst

explanation: The thalamus processes and directs almost all incoming sensory traffic to the correct region of the cerebral cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which brainstem structure contains vital autonomic centers regulating heartbeat and blood pressure?
explanation: The medulla oblongata houses cardiovascular and respiratory centers essential for basic life support. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why does damage to one side of the cerebral cortex often result in motor deficits on the opposite side of the body?

options.A: Cranial nerves decussate within the thalamus
options.B: The cerebellum inhibits ipsilateral motor pathways
options.C: Motor tracts cross over each other in the medulla oblongata
options.D: The corpus callosum blocks signals from reaching the same side

explanation: The decussation of pyramids in the medulla causes motor fibers to cross over, meaning the left hemisphere controls the right side of the body and vice versa. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary physiological function of the cerebellum?

options.A: Relaying visual and auditory sensory signals
options.B: Coordinating balance and fine-tuning motor activity
options.C: Generating conscious thought and executive reasoning
options.D: Regulating core body temperature and hunger

explanation: The cerebellum monitors and adjusts motor commands to ensure smooth, coordinated movements and proper posture. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of cerebellar damage?
explanation: Cerebellar lesions disrupt muscle coordination and balance, resulting in characteristic ataxia and unsteady movements. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which meningeal layer is the innermost membrane that adheres directly to the contours of the brain?
explanation: The pia mater is a thin, delicate layer of connective tissue that closely follows every convolution of the cerebral cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary site of cerebrospinal fluid production within the brain?
explanation: Choroid plexuses located within the cerebral ventricles actively secrete cerebrospinal fluid from filtered blood plasma. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which glial cell type plays a critical role in forming and maintaining the blood-brain barrier with its foot processes?
explanation: Astrocyte foot processes wrap around brain capillaries, signaling endothelial cells to maintain tight junctions that form the blood-brain barrier. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following substances crosses the blood-brain barrier MOST easily?

options.A: Lipid-soluble molecules like oxygen and alcohol
options.D: Large protein molecules dissolved in plasma

explanation: The lipid bilayer of capillary endothelial cells allows lipid-soluble gases and drugs to diffuse readily into the brain tissue. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h7)
